solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Religious mentor baptised for all to see

blocks.note: bap. is the register abbreviation for baptised
U is the universal film certificate, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A spiritual guide was christened in public view.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a public baptism; in fact it is two abbreviations, one from parish registers and one from film ratings.
explanation.definitionFit: Bapu, meaning father, is an Indian title of respect for a revered teacher, famously given to Gandhi.

clue.text: 15 in Orkney pub — I’m keeping Sabbath inside

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece is held within another
inside places the contraction within the word for pub

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: An Orkney pub stays open on a Sunday with me in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 15 is STEELYARD, a weighing beam, so the definition asks for its Orkney name. There are two layers of nesting, one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A bismar is a type of steelyard, the weighing beam used in Orkney and Shetland.

clue.text: Court official approved one restrained before court regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: app. is an abbreviation for approved
a means one
rit. is the musical abbreviation for ritenuto, held back
the second and fourth letters of court

explanation.surface: A court official approved someone who was held back before trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restrained' sounds like a prisoner; it is the score marking ritenuto, telling players to hold back the tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparitor was an officer who served summonses for a civil or church court.

clue.text: Former leader suffering dissent with peers

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked about, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former leader is troubled by disagreement among the nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former' is part of the definition: the -ess form is now dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Presidentess is an old word for a female president, a woman who presides over a body.

clue.text: Rabbit, Ox and Ox again? Eastern years must include Tiger initially in that

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it
must include means hold within, so the selected letter goes inside the pair of abbreviations
in that says the middle chunk sits between the two halves already named, completing the run of pieces

blocks.note: a yak is a Tibetan ox
E is the abbreviation for Eastern
the first letter of Tiger
y. is the abbreviation for year
the same ox a second time

explanation.surface: Rabbit, Ox and Tiger, years of the Chinese calendar, are listed with an Eastern flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit, Ox and Tiger all look like Chinese zodiac years, but Rabbit is the definition: to rabbit is British slang for chatter on. E and Y hold T and sit between two YAKs.
explanation.definitionFit: Yakety-yak is incessant chatter, and to rabbit on is British slang for talking at length.

clue.text: Man, say, raised boy outside? It was untrue

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means lifted from bottom to top, so the word is read upwards
outside says the turned word wraps round the island

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man brought up a boy, but the story was false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, signalled by 'say'. 'It was' marks the answer as obsolete, a Spenserian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Disleal is an obsolete form of disloyal, meaning faithless or false to an allegiance.

clue.text: Find out about earlier rest break

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the words for find out wrap round the rest

blocks.note: to sus, or suss, is to work out or discover
alt is Milton's form of halt, a stop or rest; earlier marks it as an old word

explanation.surface: Discover more about an earlier pause in proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest break' reads as one phrase, a tea break; 'rest' belongs with the wordplay and 'break' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltus is a sudden leap or breach of continuity, as in an argument that jumps a step.

clue.text: Slip in places climbing bad section

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means going upward, so the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: evil means bad
s. is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: Slipping in various spots while scaling a dangerous stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In places' belongs to the definition: it marks a dialect word, used only in some regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Slive is a dialect verb meaning to slip or slide, from Old English slifan.

clue.text: Knight tucking into salmon platter

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, so the chess abbreviation goes within the fish

blocks.note: lax is a salmon, from the Scandinavian word
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight eats salmon off a serving dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating, a fine picture for the dish; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanx was a large Roman serving dish or platter, often of silver.

clue.text: Emperor’s son swats heretic cruelly

indicators.note: cruelly suggests rough treatment, so the letters get knocked into a new order

blocks.note: all twelve letters used

explanation.surface: A prince harshly strikes a heretic.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsesarevich was the eldest son and heir of a Russian tsar, the emperor of Russia.

clue.text: Aircraftsman’s after small shirt at Leuchars

indicators.note: after says the piece it follows in the clue comes second, so the order of the two parts is swapped

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
erk is RAF slang for an aircraftsman

explanation.surface: An airman follows a small shirt at a Scottish air base.
explanation.walkthrough: Leuchars is an RAF station in Fife, Scotland, which both fits the aircraftsman and signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Serk is the Scots word for a shirt or chemise, used in Fife among other places.

clue.text: One not well wrapped in faded mattress

indicators.note: something wrapped in a covering sits inside it, so these letters go within the word for faded

blocks.note: a, the indefinite article, means one
ill means unwell
passé means past its best, faded

explanation.surface: A sick person lies wrapped up on a worn-out mattress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One not well' reads as a patient, the person on the mattress; it splits into the article and the adjective, which go in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A paillasse is a thin straw-filled mattress, from the French for straw.

clue.text: Whale hunter spots colonising species — not the first

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter of the phrase before it is dropped

blocks.note: specks are small spots
a pioneer species is the first to colonise bare ground

explanation.surface: A whaler sees spots of invasive species arriving, though not the first ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonising species' is the ecologist's pioneer species; drop its P and add it to SPECKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A specksioneer is the chief harpooner on a whaling ship, the one who leads the hunt.

clue.text: Fish farm near Ukraine’s capital

indicators.note: a word's capital is its head, the opening letter

blocks.note: a mas is a farmhouse in southern France
the initial of Ukraine

explanation.surface: A fish farm stands close to Kyiv.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ukraine's capital' invites Kyiv, but here capital means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The masu is a Pacific salmon found around Japan and Korea, a species of cherry salmon.

clue.text: Cost when working with fluid dye

indicators.note: working means in operation and moving about, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The price of a liquid colouring once it is in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid' suits a dye so well it seems part of the definition, but it is anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: Old fustic is a yellow colouring extracted from the wood of a tropical American tree.

clue.text: Club’s quality white earthenware

blocks.note: an iron is a golf club, with the apostrophe s attached
tone is a quality, as of sound or colour

explanation.surface: A golf club's finish is like white pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone china is a hard, durable white pottery first made in Staffordshire.

clue.text: Balance very hard with old plough

blocks.note: steely means hard as steel
an ard is a primitive scratch plough

explanation.surface: Keeping steady is very hard when using an ancient plough.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is a weighing device with a sliding weight on an unequal-armed beam.

clue.text: Clear gray like hog’s back

blocks.note: to rid is to clear of something
Gy is the symbol for the gray, the unit of absorbed radiation dose

explanation.surface: Plain grey, like the back of a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gray' looks like a colour but is the physics unit, one joule per kilogram, with symbol Gy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hog's back is a sharp ridge of land, so something ridgy has raised crests like it.

clue.text: Log support in addition to press

blocks.note: and means in addition to
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Something holds up a log and also squashes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron is one of a pair of metal stands that hold logs in a fireplace.

clue.text: Is in a TV broadcast, simply presented

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: all seven letters used

explanation.surface: Someone on television is shown in a plain, unadorned way.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivist describes art in the naive style, deliberately childlike and unsophisticated in its depiction.

clue.text: Part ruffling a lyre bird’s feathers located here?

indicators.note: ruffling disturbs and disorders, so the following letters are mixed up

blocks.note: pt is the abbreviation for part
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Ruffling part of a lyrebird's plumage shows where its feathers grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lyre bird' tempts you to read one bird; 'a lyre' is the anagram material and 'bird's' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pteryla is one of the tracts of skin on a bird from which its feathers grow.

clue.text: Crack about one arch-traitor in Holyrood

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for crack encloses the numeral

blocks.note: a fent is a slit or opening
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A split surrounds a single great betrayer in the Scottish Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Holyrood, home of the Scottish Parliament, marks a Scots word; the arch-traitor is Satan, the fiend.
explanation.definitionFit: Fient is the Scots form of fiend, the Devil, who betrayed God in the original rebellion.

clue.text: Staff, most of them being around years

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped
being around means surrounding, so the shortened word wraps round the abbreviation

blocks.note: the word them without its last letter
yrs is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: Most of the employees have been around for years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, a picture the rest of the clue supports; it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A thyrse, or thyrsus, is the ivy-wreathed wand carried by Bacchus and his followers.

clue.text: Continued illness’s beginning in a gum infection

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter only
in places the selected letter inside the word that follows

blocks.note: cont. is the abbreviation for continued
taken as written
taken as written
the opening letter of illness

explanation.surface: A persistent illness began as an infection of the gums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continued' looks like a verb describing the illness, but it is the abbreviation used at the foot of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagium is the agent or matter that transmits a contagious disease.

clue.text: Spaced out good friend of Snow White wanting heroin

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the drug's letter, H, is removed

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
one of the seven dwarfs

explanation.surface: A dwarf, high on drugs, misses heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spaced out' and 'heroin' paint a drug picture, but the definition means full of gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Gappy means having gaps, with its parts spaced out unevenly.

clue.text: Fish round Maori settlement

blocks.note: O is round in shape
pah, also spelt pa, is a fortified Maori village

explanation.surface: A fish swims around a New Zealand village.
explanation.definitionFit: The opah, or moonfish, is a large brightly coloured ocean fish.

clue.text: Watch closely but missing old hare

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the abbreviation for old is taken out

blocks.note: to scout is to observe carefully
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Keep a close eye on an elderly hare, but it has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hare' reads as one thing; 'old' belongs to the wordplay, and 'hare' alone is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short tail of a rabbit or hare, and the word has been used for the animal itself.

clue.text: Titanic reportedly swarming with small creatures

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the sound of the word for Titanic is taken

blocks.note: titanic means huge and powerful

explanation.surface: The Titanic is said to have been crawling with tiny pests.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital T suggests the liner; it is just the adjective meaning enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Mity means infested with mites, the tiny arachnids found in cheese, flour and the like.

clue.text: One bringing about organised operatic trip

indicators.note: organised means arranged into a new order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: all twelve letters used

explanation.surface: Someone arranges an outing to the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: To precipitate something is to cause it to happen, often suddenly, so a precipitator causes events.

clue.text: Legal action idiot puts up with, losing pounds before appeal

indicators.note: losing pounds asks for the pound symbol, the letter for libra, to be removed

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
to lump it is to put up with something unwelcome
it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: A fool tolerates a lawsuit, losing money before an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' reads as a legal appeal in this courtroom surface, but it is IT, as in having it, sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumpsit was a common-law action to recover damages for breach of a promise or contract.

clue.text: Former lodging house taken by relation spending nothing?

indicators.note: spending nothing means giving up a nought, so the letter shaped like zero is removed

blocks.note: ho. is the abbreviation for house
a relation is an account or story

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' looks like a family member but is a narrative, as in relating a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostry is an archaic word for a hostelry or inn, a place where travellers stayed.

clue.text: Prosper once hospital’s in support

indicators.note: in places the hospital abbreviation inside the word for support

blocks.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A hospital once did well when it had backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is not the pronoun but the old verb to thee, to thrive; 'once' marks it as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee was an Old English verb meaning to thrive or do well, now obsolete.
